$comment: The envUI 1.0 rename map: every public name of @envsemble/envui 0.x that changed, with its 1.0 name. It is the one source for the codemods (v1-names, v1-classes), the migration guide and the search and manifest aliases. 1.0 re-exports nothing under an old name. A new name with a dot is a part of an ES module namespace: `Menu.Item` is the `Item` part of the `Menu` export. `reused` lists 0.x names that 1.0 exports again for something else: Row and RowProps, a list row in 0.x, which is List.Item in 1.0, and a layout primitive in 1.0. v1-names still renames them, as it reads 0.x code; the lint rule leaves them alone, as an import of them may be 1.0 code.

sections.exports: Old export name to new name, per entry point. Prop and other types are listed beside their components.
sections.split: Old components that became several parts: the part follows the value of one prop, which the new part no longer takes.
sections.removed: Exports that became internal or were removed in 1.0, with what to use instead. A `value` is the constant's literal, which a codemod can inline. A `transform` names the codemod that rewrites its elements, such as v1-stack for Stack: v1-names reports the export only where it is used other than as an element.
sections.props: Props of 0.x components that 1.0 removed or changed, per entry point and component, by its 1.0 name. Each literal value of a prop maps to the props that replace it, in its place: an empty object drops the prop, and a replacement prop the element already sets is kept as it is. `report` says what replaces the prop; the v1-props codemod reports it at each use whose value is not listed, such as an expression, and with a value's own `report` at each use of that value, or, with `unless`, at each use that sets none of the props it lists. `current` lists a prop's 1.0 values, which it leaves alone without a report, so it can run again over its own output. `each` holds the rules for the properties of each object in an array the prop takes, such as an organization's `name` in OrganizationSwitcher's `items`: v1-props applies them to the objects of an array written in the prop, and reports a value it can't read, such as a variable, with the prop's `report`. A rule with only a `report` is report-only: the prop keeps its name and value, and every use is reported, as for `className` on the fields, whose target moved to the root.
sections.calls: Calls whose first argument is an object with changed properties, per entry point: a function imported by name (`show`), or the method of what a hook returns (`useToast().show`). Each property has the rules of a prop in `props`. v1-props applies them to object literals and reports any other argument.
sections.render: Components whose `prop` (`as`) became 1.0's `render`, per entry point. v1-render turns `as="h2"` into `render={<h2 />}`; an expression, or a value listed in `except` with its report, is reported.
sections.structure: Elements whose 1.0 form is another element or shape, per entry point and component, rewritten by v1-structure. The first of `cases` whose `when` matches the element's literal props, and that sets every prop of `has`, applies: `element` it becomes, `props` (null drops one, "render" turns `as` into `render`, `to` and `values` rename and map it), `add` (a literal, or `{ "element": "article" }` for render={<article />}), `children` (props for direct children by component, `*` for any other, or a report), `content` (the new children, made from props: each an `element` that takes the value of the prop `children` names and the props `props` maps to it, new name to old), `wrap` and `report`. An element whose `when` props aren't literals is reported with `report`. An entry with `"transform": "v1-app-shell"` and `reports`, such as AppShell's, has no cases: that transform rewrites it, and v1-structure leaves it. An entry under a 0.x name that `exports` renames, such as ClickableCard, only reports: v1-names reports each element it renames with the `report` of the first case that matches.
sections.classes: Old class name to new name. An entry also renames every class and custom property that continues it with a hyphen (env-date-time-well becomes env-date-picker-well, --env-notice-tone becomes --env-alert-tone); the longest matching entry wins.
sections.classAttributes: Modifier classes that became attributes on their root class: `class` the root and `attributes` the data- attributes, an empty value testing presence. v1-classes rewrites selectors with the specificity they had and reports the classes in markup, which the component's props set now.
sections.classesWithin: Class renames that depend on an ancestor, by the ancestor's old class: 0.7's DiffCount labelled itself with the counter's label class, which 1.0's DiffStat names for itself. In a selector that puts the old class inside the ancestor, such as `.env-diff-count .env-counter-label`, the class takes this name instead of the one in classes. Markup is not changed by context: a className is renamed by classes alone.
sections.classReports: Classes that 1.0 neither keeps nor renames, and selectors that no longer match, which v1-classes leaves as they are and reports with `report`, what to use instead. An entry without `within` covers its 0.x class and every class that continues it with a hyphen, which no shorter entry in classes renames. An entry with `within` names 1.0 classes: v1-classes reports, after the renames, a selector that puts the class inside the `within` class, as `.env-document-tabs-tab:hover .env-document-tabs-close`. An entry with `attributes` names a 1.0 class and the attributes 1.0 no longer sets on it: v1-classes reports, after the renames, a selector that puts one of them on the class, as `.env-panel-dock[data-chips]`.
sections.docs: Old documentation page slug (docs/components/<slug>.md and the catalogue route components/<slug>) to the new one.
sections.tokens: Every custom property that envUI 0.x or 1.0’s development defined and 1.0 no longer does, with what replaces it: `to`, the 1.0 custom property, which v1-classes writes in its place (every token takes the --env- prefix, and a few names change beyond it); `value`, the color of a 0.7 fixed color that no token replaces, which v1-classes reports; or `removed`, with `to` what to use instead where there is one, which v1-classes also reports. A `note` says what changed beyond the name. `npm run tokens:build` writes this section from packages/ui/src/generated/token-migration.json.
